text:
kate-support: @dylan-sre heads up — ACME reported missing spans in Trace View for a set of request IDs. customer says links from request_id -> trace are broken intermittently. screenshot: https://acme.screenshots/trace-missing.png

acme-dev: repro steps below, happens in prod intermittently. starts when we enable streaming on /generate. a sample request_id: 8d9f6b2a-ff34-4c21-9a7b-77b2e1c4b9a1. trace url they see: https://console.redwood.ai/traces?request_id=8d9f6b2a

acme-dev: curl to repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Request-ID: 8d9f6b2a-ff34-4c21-9a7b-77b2e1c4b9a1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

kate-support: customer says the backend logs have the request id and the model worker logs show work done, but the trace view stops after the gateway span. no spans from inference nodes.

maya-cs: escalated via support ticket #4521, customer is worried about missing billing evidence (they need full trace for audit). limited impact but hits legal.

dylan-sre: can you paste a few raw request headers (sanitized)? also what deployment mode — hosted/dedicated/private?

acme-dev: deployed on dedicated in us-west. headers we forward: "x-request-id": 8d9f6..., "x-forwarded-for": 10.2.1.5, "x-redwood-trace": not present by default (we tried adding but no change).

alin-ml: quick hypothesis — streaming responses open a chunked connection and our proxy strips/renames trace propagation header when switching to the streaming backend. I've seen similar when the connection is hijacked for SSE. if the frontend writes a new trace header after proxy upgrade the backend tracer doesn't pick it up.

dylan-sre: interesting — we also recently rolled a change in the routing proxy (PR #8142) that rewrites incoming headers for traffic to Dedicated pools. might be related. i'll check proxy logs for header rewrite events around the customer's timestamps (they provided three example timestamps).

perf-bot: [deploy] routing-proxy v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 deployed at 1770001200 (sha: a3f9c2).

dylan-sre: ok that matches. potential root cause: header rename + sampling mismatch = orphaned traces (request_id logged but not linked to trace). workaround: add an explicit propagation header to the request: "X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id>" — customer can inject for now.

kate-support: can we get a short repro we can patch into a staging route? acme-dev volunteered to run test on a dedicated test pool.

acme-dev: we can run it midday PST. will send times. happy to run a weave of 50 streamed requests.

alin-ml: next steps: (1) dylan to confirm header rewrite behavior and create a failing test that shows dropped spans, (2) if reproduced, add fix in proxy to preserve trace header during streaming handoff, (3) temporary console change to link by request_id when trace missing (low-risk UX patch), (4) inform customer with special repro build.

dylan-sre: logging ticket created: INF-2209 with attached proxy logs. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. ETA for hotfix: 48-72h if repro is solid.

maya-cs: I'll update the customer with the workaround and ETA. keeping legal in the loop. :thumbsup:

kate-support: thanks everyone. please drop updates in this thread. if dylan needs access to the customer's dedicated pool creds, i'll coordinate offline.

dylan-sre: quick note — also saw one case where request_id length >36 chars caused our trace linker to bail (regex mismatch). adding that to INF-2209 as a secondary vector.

alin-ml: good catch. we'll add a normalizer to accept UUID-like or extended ids.

perf-bot: incident-note: INF-2209 created by dylan-sre at 1770002500.

kate-support: closing loop for now — customer ok with workaround, will run tests tomorrow. updating ticket and adding reproduction artifacts. :white_check_mark:
